title: Optimization Design Matrix
description: The pre-registered plan for an optimization-campaign iteration (design spec 5.5). Written BEFORE any config is executed: rows, generator/alias structure, and a randomized-but-recorded run order so time-ordered drift (thermal effects, cache warming) cannot masquerade as a factor effect. See orchestrator.optimize.matrix.matrix_payload.

factor_ids.description: Declared factor ids in design-column order, e.g. ["A", "B", "C"].

kind.description: Design family. "fractional" designs carry non-empty aliases; "central_composite" adds axial/center points for curvature.

resolution.description: Design resolution (III/IV/V) for a fractional design; null for a full factorial or central composite, which have no aliasing to report at this level.

generators.description: Base-column index tuples defining each derived factor's generator, e.g. [[0, 1, 2]] means the 4th factor = product of base columns 0, 1, 2. Empty for a full factorial.

aliases.description: Confounded term-label pairs, e.g. [["AB", "C"]] means the AB interaction is aliased with (indistinguishable from) main effect C. Empty means every main effect and two-factor interaction is separately estimable (resolution-V or full factorial). A fractional design's caveat must survive into this artifact rather than being silently dropped.

run_order.description: A permutation of row indices [0, len(rows)) giving the randomized execution order.

run_order_seed.description: RNG seed that reproduces run_order from orchestrator.optimize.matrix.randomized_run_order — recorded so the randomization is reproducible, not just random.

run_timeout_sec.description: Wall-clock ceiling, in seconds, that EVERY row of this matrix was measured under -- optimization.run_timeout_sec resolved through stage_runner.resolve_run_timeout, defaulting to 600. Recorded whether or not the campaign declared it, because "the author did not choose" and "the author chose 600" produce identical runs: without this field, a failed row reading "timed out after 600 seconds" cannot be told apart from the same campaign re-launched at a different ceiling. A resolved run parameter that shaped the measurement belongs on the pre-registration, not only in a campaign file that may since have been revised for the next epoch.

workload_seeds.description: Map of row_index (as a string) -> the workload seed exported into that row's run, present only when the campaign declares optimization.workload.seed_env (spec 3.7 oracle 3, 3.8). Written by stage_runner._assign_workload_seeds BEFORE this matrix is registered, so the seeds are pre-registered draws rather than an after-the-fact log.

paired.description: True on a confirm-round matrix under common random numbers: replicate i of EVERY finalist ran the same seed, so the draw's contribution cancels out of the finalist-to-finalist difference and certificate.terminal_regret_bound reads the paired differences (bonferroni_one_sided_t_paired) instead of Welch-combining two independent variances. Absent at the spending stages, where a seed shared across the block would confound the entire fit with one workload draw.

held_fixed.description: Map of factor id -> the level it was pinned at for this matrix, for factors that are declared in the campaign but not columns of THIS design (e.g. a factor dropped after screening). Recorded because a row's levels alone cannot distinguish "this factor was not varied" from "this factor was not present".

policy_hash.description: Content hash of the compiled policy.json that scheduled this matrix. Provenance: a reader can check that this design was produced under the pre-registration that was hashed before the first benchmark run, and not a later one -- the same hash transitions.jsonl records per row.

row_index.description: Position in the design matrix, matching orchestrator.optimize.matrix.ConfigRow.row_index. This is the join key against runs.jsonl for fidelity checking.

levels.description: Map of factor id -> the real-world level this row runs at, e.g. {"A": "low", "B": 4}.

role.description: Design-point role: a full/fractional-factorial corner, a replicated center point (supplies the pure-error estimate), or a central-composite axial/star point (supplies curvature).

replicate.description: Replicate index for repeated points (e.g. the 3rd center-point replicate has replicate=2); 0 for unreplicated corners.

apply.description: The rendered, mechanical instructions for making this row's levels take effect on the target — no model call is involved in producing this.

cli_args.description: CLI flags to pass to the target's invocation, e.g. ["--queues=4"].

factor_id.description: The factor this patch renders. Carried so the REALIZED patch can be keyed by factor in the row's applied_patches, which is what makes it addressable from a manipulation predicate (predicates resolve dotted paths through dicts only -- a list of patches could not be addressed at all).

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer to the field to replace, e.g. "/cache/policy" or "/tiers/0/bytes" (~0 escapes a literal ~, ~1 a literal /). Must address a field that already exists: a config_patch replaces a value the target reads, it never creates structure.

patches.description: Config-file patches (apply.kind: config_patch). Each is applied to a PER-RUN COPY of `path` -- the campaign author's file is never mutated -- and the copy's path is substituted for every occurrence of `path` in the assembled run command, so `path` must appear as an argument value in optimization.run_command. `pointer` is an RFC 6901 JSON pointer addressing an existing field; `value` keeps its declared type (an int stays an int). What was realized per run is recorded separately as the row's applied_patches.

center_choice_pinned.description: Optional map of factor id -> true for a choice-typed factor pinned to its low level at a center point (a choice factor has no interior, so a center row still needs a concrete level).
